newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower while calls on pork bellies ranged from 0.200 cent a lb lower to 0.100 higher, livestock analysts said.

Although some analysts still expected light hog marketings to underpin both cash and futures markets, most analysts say hog futures will be pressured as packers keep bids for cash hogs down and cut kills. The weak tone to cash pork prices and unexpected weakness in cash loins should keep packers bids from rising, they said.
The latest CME lean index was down $0.42 to $84.03 per cwt.

Some analysts cited weakness in cash belly prices even in the face of recent light slaughter levels and expect this to weigh on pork belly futures. However, others still look for short covering support ahead of Tuesday's monthly U.S. Cold Storage report, they said. USDA quoted 12-14 lb bellies down $1.00 at $83.00 per cwt Monday.

Even though the weekly CME Out-of-Town report, also Tuesday afternoon, will likely show a net in-movement, most indications on USDA's monthly Cold Storage report pointed to an exceptional out-movement of pork bellies for the month.
Belly futures also held a major trend line Monday on the early break and light hog kills will keep offerings tight, sources said.

Indications on Tuesday's Cold Storage report ranged from 52.2 million to 59 million lbs in U.S. warehouses on May 1 compared with 54.8 million on hand April 1 and 57.2 million in storage May 1 of last year. Net storings estimtes ranged from out 2.64 million to in 4.16 million lbs and compared with the 10-year average net in product movement of 9.8 million lbs.
Estimates on the CME Out-of-Town report ranged from in 250,000 to 1.0 million lbs compared with in movement of 836,000 lbs last week and in 2.482 million lbs last year.
